vcmi.lobby.mapGen.help:
{MapGen}

Our own random map generator with every one of its settings: the map, biomes, borders, treasure, monsters, underground, scenery and water. Generate makes a map and selects it in the scenario list.
vcmi.mapGen.tab.subtitle: Every setting of our own map generator
vcmi.mapGen.defaults.help:
{Defaults}

Puts every setting back to the Nostalgia defaults. The default. Calibrated against the random maps you have played: biome rims, treasure, mines, towns, monsters and terrain at the rates those maps carry.
vcmi.mapGen.generate.help:
{Generate map}

Makes a map from these settings and selects it in the scenario list. Settings are saved as you change them.
vcmi.mapGen.generate.humans: Generating a map for %d human players...
vcmi.mapGen.generate.failed: The map generator failed. See extmapgen_log.txt in the VCMI logs folder.
vcmi.mapGen.template.none: No template: free layout, tuned to Nostalgia's numbers
vcmi.mapGen.map.size.help:
{Map size}

S 36, M 72, L 108, XL 144, H 180, XH 216 or G 252 cells a side. A new hero crosses one corner to corner in about 3, 6, 10, 13, 16, 19 or 23 days, over open grass with nothing in the way.
vcmi.mapGen.map.underground.help:
{Underground}

A second, underground level linked to the surface by subterranean gates.
vcmi.mapGen.map.declareMods.help:
{Use mod content}

Place modded terrain, creature banks and dwellings from your installed mods, and declare them in the map so VCMI requires the same mods to open it. Off makes a map that loads anywhere, core content only.
vcmi.mapGen.map.players.help:
{Players}

How many players the map has, human and computer together.
vcmi.mapGen.map.humans.help:
{Human players}

How many of those seats a human can take. The rest are computer players.
vcmi.mapGen.map.template.help:
{Template}

The biome layout. Free layout is our own, calibrated on your own random maps; the game's templates (Jebus Cross, Coldshadow's Fantasy and the rest) lay the biomes out their way, with the settings on the other pages still applied.
vcmi.mapGen.map.size.s0.help:
{Small, 36x36}

A new hero crosses it corner to corner in about 3 days over open grass, with nothing in the way. A cobblestone road halves that; rough ground, sand, snow and swamp stretch it.

vcmi.mapGen.zoneCells.help:
{Biome size}

Map cells per biome. Larger biomes mean fewer, bigger areas to fight over.
vcmi.mapGen.zoneCap.help:
{Most biomes per level}

Upper limit on biomes per level, player starts included. Biome size decides how many biomes a map naturally wants; this only matters if you pull it below that to force fewer, bigger biomes.
vcmi.mapGen.highLootRatio.help:
{Treasure biomes}

Share of the non-start biomes that are rich, heavily guarded treasure biomes.
vcmi.mapGen.townRatio.help:
{Neutral town biomes}

Share of the non-start biomes built around a neutral town. Large maps add more towns by area.
vcmi.mapGen.lowLootRatio.help:
{Open low-loot biomes}

Share of the non-start biomes that are open ground with resource generators and weaker loot.
vcmi.mapGen.borderSolidity.help:
{Border solidity}

How biomes are walled off: solid rims with thick lobes, a plain band, porous thin walls, or no border scenery at all.
vcmi.mapGen.biomeWobble.help:
{Border wobble}

How much biome borders bend. 0 gives straight lines.
vcmi.mapGen.interconnectivity.help:
{Biome connections}

How many neighbouring biomes get a passage between them.
vcmi.mapGen.interconnectPortal.help:
{Portal share}

Share of the passages that are two-way portals instead of open ground.
vcmi.mapGen.openPathNoRoad.help:
{Passages without road}

Weight of plain open passages among the non-portal ones.
vcmi.mapGen.openPathRoad.help:
{Passages with road}

Weight of roaded passages among the non-portal ones.
vcmi.mapGen.roadNetwork.help:
{Build Road Network}

Roads linking every town. Off leaves only the roads through passages.
vcmi.mapGen.roadType.help:
{Road type}

What the roads are paved with. A hero moves along cobblestone for half the cost of open ground, along gravel for 65 and along dirt for 75 of every 100. Real random maps pave almost every road with cobblestone.
vcmi.mapGen.artifactDensity.help:
{Artifacts}

How many artifacts lie on the map.
vcmi.mapGen.artifactRichness.help:
{Artifact quality}

Shifts artifacts from treasure and minor toward major and relic.
vcmi.mapGen.pickupDensity.help:
{Chests and campfires}

Multiplier on treasure chests, spell scrolls and campfires.
vcmi.mapGen.resourceDensity.help:
{Resource piles}

Multiplier on loose resource piles.
vcmi.mapGen.mineDensity.help:
{Mines}

Multiplier on mines beyond each player's starting pair.
vcmi.mapGen.starterMines.help:
{Starting mines}

A sawmill and an ore pit beside every start.
vcmi.mapGen.dwellingDensity.help:
{Creature dwellings}

Multiplier on external creature dwellings.
vcmi.mapGen.bonusDensity.help:
{Shrines and bonuses}

Multiplier on shrines, schools, stat and luck buildings.
vcmi.mapGen.monsterStrength.help:
{Monster tier}

Creature levels added to every monster: weaker, lower-level creatures or stronger, higher-level ones.
vcmi.mapGen.stackScale.help:
{Stack size}

Creatures per stack. Low-level creatures come in big stacks and high-level ones in small stacks; this moves the whole scale up or down together. At 1.0x the game rolls each creature's own usual number.
vcmi.mapGen.guardDensity.help:
{Monster count}

Multiplier on every biome's monster budget, guards and roamers together.
vcmi.mapGen.objectGuardShare.help:
{Guarding vs roaming}

Share of each biome's monsters posted on something worth taking; the rest roam.
vcmi.mapGen.guardTreasure.help:
{Guards on treasure}

Monsters standing on artifacts, chests, Pandora's boxes, prisons, banks and other treasure. Off leaves treasure unguarded; those monsters roam instead.
vcmi.mapGen.guardMines.help:
{Guards on mines}

Monsters standing on mines and other resource generators.
vcmi.mapGen.guardDwellings.help:
{Guards on dwellings}

Monsters standing on creature dwellings.
vcmi.mapGen.guardBottlenecks.help:
{Guards at bottlenecks}

Monsters standing in the passages between biomes.
vcmi.mapGen.chokeGuardRatio.help:
{Bottleneck guard share}

Share of biome passages with a monster standing in them, when bottleneck guards are on.
vcmi.mapGen.guardPortals.help:
{Guards at portals}

A monster in front of each two-way monolith that links two biomes.
vcmi.mapGen.lootGuardWeight.help:
{Treasure guard pull}

How strongly guards gather on treasure and dwellings compared with the rates measured on your random maps.
vcmi.mapGen.mineGuardWeight.help:
{Mine guard pull}

How strongly guards gather on mines compared with the rates measured on your random maps.
vcmi.mapGen.subterraneanGateRatio.help:
{Gates between levels}

How many subterranean gates link the surface and the underground.
vcmi.mapGen.subterraneanNarrow.help:
{Narrow tunnels}

Share of underground biomes carved as narrow tunnels rather than open caverns.
vcmi.mapGen.subterraneanOpen.help:
{Open cave floor}

Share of the underground left walkable.
vcmi.mapGen.decorDensity.help:
{Scenery}

Multiplier on scenery inside biomes (mountains, trees, rocks). Border scenery follows Border solidity.
vcmi.mapGen.riverAmount.help:
{River amount}

Multiplier on how much of the map the rivers run through. 1 is the share measured on real random maps.
vcmi.mapGen.teams.help:
{Teams}

Allied teams among the players, dealt out in colour order: red, blue, tan and so on in turn. None is every player for themselves; a count at or above the number of players is the same.
vcmi.mapGen.waterCoverage.help:
{Amount of water}

Share of the surface under water. 0 is a dry map. The land left over is shared out among the biomes.
vcmi.mapGen.waterShape.help:
{Water layout}

Where the water goes. Lakes: a few inland lakes, with land all along the map edge. Coastal: a sea along one side of the map. Starts on that side move inland. Continental: sea all around the map edge and one land mass in the middle. Starts move inland onto it. Mediterranean: a sea in the middle of the map with land all around it. Highland: many small lakes scattered through the land. Islands: every player on an island of their own, with open sea between. Each player starts with a shipyard and a boat on the shore, and boats are the only way across. The straits take water of their own, so a small amount comes out higher. Archipelago: many islands, every player on one of their own and the rest neutral, waiting for whoever sails there first. Needs about a quarter of a small map under water.
vcmi.mapGen.waterAccess.help:
{Harbours}

Where heroes can take to the water. Starts: a shipyard at each player start on the shore. Towns: a shipyard in every biome with a town on the shore, as the game's own generator does. Every biome: a boat in every other biome on the shore as well. Lakes under 25 cells get none. On Islands and Archipelago every player still gets a shipyard and a boat at the start, whatever this says.
vcmi.mapGen.waterTreasure.help:
{Treasure on the water}

Multiplier on what lies on the water a boat can reach: flotsam, sea chests, survivors and the two water banks, the shipwreck and the derelict ship.
vcmi.mapGen.waterBuildings.help:
{Buildings on the water}

Multiplier on the sites a boat can visit: mermaids and buoys for luck and morale, sirens, and whirlpools, which come in pairs and throw a ship from one to the other.
